speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help narrow this down, have you had any close contact with anyone who recently developed a similar rash or had an eye infection?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). The clinical presentation of a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, preceded by a viral prodrome (fever, rhinorrhea, headache), followed specifically by a facial rash that spares the perioral area, is the classic "slapped cheek" appearance of Parvovirus B19 infection.
